explanation: Infrastructure as code describes the environment in files that tools deploy, and an SDN controller separates the control plane so a central program configures the devices through an API. Spanning tree prevents loops, port mirroring copies traffic and a console server gives out-of-band access, but none of them automates configuration.
options: Port mirroring from each switch to a central analyzer
Spanning tree with a lower root bridge priority
Infrastructure as code templates kept in version control
A software-defined networking controller with an API
A console server cabled to every device

stem: An administrator wants to discover which hosts are up on a subnet and which TCP ports each one has open. Which tool is built for this?
explanation: Nmap scans for live hosts, open ports, services and operating systems. Use it only on networks you are authorized to scan.

stem: An audit finds routers still managed over TCP 23, which sends passwords in cleartext. Which protocol and port should replace it?
explanation: TCP 23 is Telnet. SSH on port 22 gives the same command-line access with encryption and stronger authentication. HTTP, TFTP and SNMPv1 are all unencrypted.

stem: A company hosts a mail server at 10.0.0.25 and needs it reachable from the internet at the fixed public address 203.0.113.25. Which NAT type fits?
explanation: Static NAT creates a permanent one-to-one mapping, so connections to the public address always reach the same internal server. PAT is for many hosts sharing one address for outbound traffic.

stem: Voice calls between offices break up whenever large file transfers run across the WAN. Which two changes would help most? (Choose two.)
explanation: QoS gives voice priority in the queues, and more bandwidth or moving bulk transfers reduces congestion. Voice over TCP would add retransmission delay, and jitter buffers smooth delay, so turning them off hurts.
options: Add WAN bandwidth or schedule bulk transfers off hours
Turn on jumbo frames on the IP phones
Use QoS to mark and prioritize voice traffic
Turn off the phones' jitter buffers
Change the phones to send voice over TCP

stem: Printed network diagrams with IP addresses and device names were found in an office recycling bin outside the building. Which attack does this invite, and what prevents it?
explanation: Attackers search trash for diagrams, passwords and other details that help plan an attack. Shredding or secure disposal of sensitive documents stops it.
options: Phishing, prevented by email filtering at the gateway
Tailgating, prevented by an access control vestibule
Shoulder surfing, prevented by privacy screens on monitors
Dumpster diving, prevented by shredding sensitive paper

stem: Two firewalls both pass traffic at the same time and share the load. If one fails, the other carries everything at reduced capacity. What is this design?
explanation: In active-active both units carry traffic, which uses all the hardware but means each must have spare capacity. In active-passive one unit waits idle until the active one fails.

stem: A load balancer chooses a back-end server using only the IP addresses and TCP port numbers of each connection, without reading the HTTP request. At which OSI layer is it balancing?
explanation: Decisions based on addresses and port numbers are Layer 4 load balancing. A Layer 7 load balancer reads application data such as URLs, headers or cookies before choosing a server.

stem: A small campus has an access layer and one pair of switches that does both the core and the distribution work. What is this design called?
explanation: A collapsed core (two-tier) design merges the core and distribution layers into one, which saves cost where a separate core is not needed. Larger campuses keep three tiers.

stem: How does an access port differ from a trunk port?
explanation: An access port belongs to one data VLAN (plus an optional voice VLAN) and connects end devices. A trunk carries many VLANs with 802.1Q tags between switches, routers and hypervisors.
options: An access port carries every VLAN with tags
An access port carries one data VLAN untagged
An access port can connect only to routers
An access port has no MAC address table

stem: An access point in the 5 GHz band is set to 80 MHz channel width instead of 20 MHz. What is the trade-off?
explanation: Channel bonding joins adjacent 20 MHz channels for higher data rates, but it leaves fewer separate channels, so dense deployments often use 20 or 40 MHz.
options: More throughput per client, but fewer channels for neighbors
Longer range, but only 802.11b clients can connect
Fewer clients allowed, but no change in throughput
Better security, but a lower data rate for each client

stem: A team gathers in a meeting room and talks through what each person would do if the main data center flooded, without touching any systems. What kind of exercise is this?
explanation: A tabletop exercise walks through a scenario in discussion to check plans and roles. Validation tests actually fail over systems to prove the plan works.

stem: A web server runs software with a known flaw, and attack code that uses the flaw is public. In security terms, what is the attack code?
explanation: The flaw is the vulnerability, the code that takes advantage of it is the exploit, and risk is the chance and impact of it being used. A threat actor is the person or group behind an attack.

stem: A technician wants to see which ports a server is listening on and which connections are established right now. Which command shows this?
explanation: netstat (or ss on newer Linux systems) lists listening ports and active connections with their states. ping tests reachability and nslookup queries DNS.

stem: A router can reach its directly connected networks but no remote network that it has no specific route for. Which entry is most likely missing from its table?
explanation: Without a default route (gateway of last resort), a router drops packets for any destination not in its table. Check it with a command such as show ip route or route print.

stem: Switches download their firmware from a server with a simple file transfer protocol that has no login and runs on UDP 69. Which protocol is it?
explanation: TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) uses UDP 69 and has no authentication, so it should be limited to trusted management networks. SFTP runs over SSH on 22, FTP uses 20 and 21, and SMB uses 445.

stem: A technician pings 127.0.0.1 on a workstation and gets replies. What does that prove?
explanation: 127.0.0.0/8 is the loopback range, and traffic to it never leaves the host. A reply shows the IP stack works, but says nothing about the cable, gateway or DNS.
options: The local TCP/IP stack is working
The DNS server is answering queries

stem: Which Ethernet mode still uses CSMA/CD and can suffer collisions?
explanation: In half duplex a device either sends or receives, so it listens before sending and backs off after collisions. Full duplex sends and receives at the same time on separate pairs, so collisions do not happen.

stem: Why should a server room's humidity not be kept too low?
explanation: Low humidity lets static build up and discharge into components. High humidity risks condensation and corrosion, so data centers keep humidity in a middle range.
options: Dry air blocks wireless signals in the room
Dry air causes condensation on the equipment
Dry air makes fiber optic cables lose signal
Dry air raises the risk of electrostatic discharge

stem: A company's internal DNS server receives a query for a website it does not host and works through root, TLD and other servers to find the answer for the client. What role is it playing?
explanation: A recursive resolver does the full lookup for the client and caches the answer. An authoritative server answers only for zones it hosts.

stem: A firewall rule list ends without any rule matching a packet. What happens to the packet on most firewalls?
explanation: Firewalls and ACLs end with an implicit deny: anything not explicitly allowed is blocked. That is why the needed traffic has to be permitted on purpose.
options: It is dropped by the implicit deny
It is logged and then forwarded
It is allowed by the implicit permit
It is sent back to the source

stem: A Windows host cannot reach its gateway, and the technician wants to see what MAC address the host has stored for the gateway's IP. Which command shows this?
explanation: arp -a shows the ARP cache, the IP-to-MAC mappings the host has learned. An unexpected MAC for the gateway can point to ARP poisoning or a duplicate address.

stem: Which measurement does ping report that helps diagnose latency?
explanation: Ping reports how long each echo takes to come back (round-trip time), plus packet loss. Traceroute is the tool for hops.

stem: Which traffic type exists in IPv4 but is not used in IPv6?
explanation: IPv6 has no broadcast. Functions that used broadcast in IPv4, such as finding a neighbor's MAC address, use multicast groups instead, for example the solicited-node multicast address.

stem: A video site wants users in many countries to load large files quickly without every request crossing an ocean to its origin servers. Which service fits?
explanation: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users, which cuts latency and offloads the origin. A VPN secures connections, and QoS prioritizes traffic, but neither moves content closer to users.

stem: Two OSPF routes to the same prefix have costs of 20 and 30. What does the router do?
explanation: Within one protocol the lower metric wins, so the cost 20 route is used. Administrative distance only compares routes from different sources, and equal-cost routes would both be installed.

stem: A park needs Wi-Fi in places with no cable runs. Some access points have a wired uplink, and the rest relay traffic to them wirelessly. Which design is this?
explanation: In a mesh network, access points connect to each other wirelessly and relay traffic toward the ones with wired backhaul. Ad hoc networks connect clients directly with no access point.

stem: A contract says the provider must keep the WAN service available 99.9 percent of the month and pay credits if it does not. What is this document?
explanation: An SLA sets measurable service levels, such as uptime and response times, and the remedies when they are missed. An MOU states intent and is usually less binding.

stem: Employees bring their own phones to work. How should the network treat these devices?
explanation: BYOD devices are not fully managed, so a separate segment with only the access they need limits risk while still letting staff use them.
options: Give them the same rights as company laptops
Put them on a separate segment with limited access
Join them to the server VLAN for faster access
Block them from every network including guest

stem: A switch port shows as administratively down. What does that mean?
explanation: Administratively down means the port was shut down in the configuration and must be enabled. A port that is down for physical reasons shows as down or not connected instead.
options: Someone disabled the port in its configuration
The cable at the far end is unplugged
The port detected a security violation
The connected device has a duplex mismatch

stem: Hosts on VLAN 30 at one site cannot reach VLAN 30 hosts on the switch across the trunk, but VLAN 10 works. What should be checked?
explanation: Trunks can be limited to a list of allowed VLANs. If VLAN 30 is missing from the allowed list, or not created on the far switch, its traffic does not cross.
options: Whether the hosts use the same DNS server
Whether VLAN 30 is allowed on the trunk
